findings.title: Cover inspect-records traversal and symlink rejection
findings.why_it_matters: The recursive projects-root scan has no CLI integration coverage for nested records, hidden directories or symlink rejection. A future traversal regression could read outside the selected root; no current bypass is asserted.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added inspect-records traversal in bin/daily-tasks.mjs:33-52 promises nested traversal, hidden-directory exclusion and symlink rejection in skills/daily-tasks/references/cli.md:27, but inspection of test/integration.test.mjs and a search of every test/evaluation .mjs file found no inspect-records invocation, confirming the behavioral coverage gap for a projectsRoot containing nested records or symlinks; production incidence was not measured and no current boundary bypass is asserted.

findings.first_evidence: lib/reconciliation/reconciliation.mjs:91 --   if (byId.size !== cloned.length) throw new TypeError('Duplicate record identities must be resolved first');
findings.suggested_fix: Check for one matching record only when resolving a changed ID, affected blocker target or traversed ancestor. Preserve unrelated duplicates unchanged. findings.title: Scope duplicate checks to affected reopening records
findings.why_it_matters: A copied Markdown record can preserve its hidden UUID. Two unrelated records sharing an ID make reopening a healthy task fail before its unambiguous ancestry is traversed, violating affected-record conflict isolation. The reproduction establishes reachability, not production incidence or random UUID collisions.
findings.validation_reason: On reviewed HEAD 11fd3dc plus its current working-tree changes, a read-only Node v24.19.0/win32 reproduction returned both completed parent IDs for an unambiguous reopened task but threw 'Duplicate record identities must be resolved first' after adding two unrelated project records sharing another ID, because the newly added lib/reconciliation/reconciliation.mjs:91 rejects the entire inventory before traversing changedIds, contrary to docs/requirements.md:26 and the check-in skill's conflict isolation rule; bin/daily-tasks.mjs:24 exposes that inventory directly, establishing reachability, while production incidence was not measured.

requirements.assessment: Bounded skills, accepted priorities and automatic carry-forward.
Explicit individual or batch acceptance; manual rows remain candidates.
Authoritative records and per-view reconciliation exist; unrelated identity conflicts still block reopening (#2).
UUIDv7 identity, hidden references and links exist; duplicate isolation has defect #2.
Flat milestone layout, milestone DoD and Markdown views supplied.
Optional PARA integration and explicit document-maturity compatibility are present.
Human owner authority and optional stable assignee are distinct.
Lifecycle, explicit activity, UTC storage and local display rules are supplied.
Informational dependencies and independent shared blockers are supplied.
Closure checks and explicit child cancellation dispositions are supplied.
Reopening and move protocol exist; unrelated duplicates can prevent parent reopening (#2).
Resumable local-day check-in, recovery and carry-forward exist; independent reopening is affected by #2.
Explicit configuration roots, user/timezone/priorities and storage paths are supplied.
Script-only append/query/archive, corrections and retry deduplication are supplied.
Pure integrity/recovery proposals and narrow log mutation preserve skill-owned Markdown authoring.

implementation_units.assessment: Shared contract, canonical skills and portable identity are present.
Decision-log interface and behavioral tests are present.
Integrity, reconciliation and recovery are implemented with scoped reopening defect #2.
All six routed skills are present.
PARA compatibility, version update and evaluation scenarios are present; no user-note migration is implied.
Adapters, checks, tests and evaluation harness are present; scanner coverage needs #1. Final independent evaluation and publication follow this review by caller instruction.

requirements_completeness.reverse_check: Checked the explicit handoff plan and canonical skills, helpers and coordinated diffs. No additional unrequested behavior rule established. Partial statuses refer to existing findings #1/#2, not omitted implementation units. Native host activation remains unverified; final independent evaluation and publication are caller work after review.

peer.coverage: adversarial lens: in-process fallback (cross-model peer not run: Windows runner access failure before any job ID; automatic approval review rejected same-route escalation because external Claude transfer lacked destination-specific authorization). No content sent; no job outstanding.

verdicts.reason: The newly added inspect-records traversal in bin/daily-tasks.mjs:33-52 promises nested traversal, hidden-directory exclusion and symlink rejection in skills/daily-tasks/references/cli.md:27, but inspection of test/integration.test.mjs and a search of every test/evaluation .mjs file found no inspect-records invocation, confirming the behavioral coverage gap for a projectsRoot containing nested records or symlinks; production incidence was not measured and no current boundary bypass is asserted.

On reviewed HEAD 11fd3dc plus its current working-tree changes, a read-only Node v24.19.0/win32 reproduction returned both completed parent IDs for an unambiguous reopened task but threw 'Duplicate record identities must be resolved first' after adding two unrelated project records sharing another ID, because the newly added lib/reconciliation/reconciliation.mjs:91 rejects the entire inventory before traversing changedIds, contrary to docs/requirements.md:26 and the check-in skill's conflict isolation rule; bin/daily-tasks.mjs:24 exposes that inventory directly, establishing reachability, while production incidence was not measured.

Although scripts/write-capabilities.mjs:5-13 duplicates operation names from bin/daily-tasks.mjs:12-31, a read-only comparison of the current CLI --help output with capabilities.json on reviewed HEAD 11fd3dc plus working-tree changes under Node v24.19.0/win32 found all 18 names identical, so the alleged failure requires a hypothetical future unsynchronized edit and the inspected evidence establishes a refactoring preference rather than a current contract mismatch.

validation.evidence_basis: No quote-anchored independent cross-model corroboration; all three selected findings received verdicts in the single bounded batch.
